titleEn: Not Just Bread—Soup Too! Yum, Yum!

pages.text: "I don't like carrots!" Coco picked the carrots out of the soup. In the kitchen behind the bakery, Coco, a little mouse in a red headscarf, ate only bits of bread. The next batch was turning golden in the oven, the big fiery place where bread bakes.

"I don't like beans either!" Coco picked out every bean and took more bread. "Tomorrow morning, I'll carry the first basket of bread!" Bakery Mom, with flour on her arms, looked at the bowl full of carrots. Her eyebrows drooped.

The next morning, Coco tried to lift the first bread basket. Their front paws trembled. The basket wouldn't rise. "Huh? Why is it so heavy?" Grandpa Mole, who bought the first bread every morning, waited by the door.
Mom called Coco to the dough table. There were two bowls. "This has just flour. This dough has water and salt too." Mom covered both bowls with towels, then sat beside Grandpa to wait.

Mom lifted the towels. The bowl of flour was still powder. The dough with everything added had risen to twice its size, soft and fluffy. "Ho ho! It rises when you put everything in," said Grandpa, poking the risen dough.

Mom whispered in Coco's ear. "Your body is like dough. With only bread, it stays like plain flour. Add carrots and beans too, and your strength can rise." Then she sang, "Not just bread—soup too! Yum, yum!" Coco gulped.

That evening, Coco bit into a carrot with their front teeth. Crunch! "...Oh? Carrots in soup are sweet!" Coco chewed and swallowed the beans one by one, until the bowl was empty. "Not just bread—soup too! Yum, yum!"
Coco puffed out their chest. "Now I can do it!" Up went the first bread basket! Their front paws didn't tremble at all. "Grandpa, I'll carry it!" Grandpa smiled wide.
Now Coco knew the dinner promise. "One, a bite of bread! Two, a bite of soup! Three, carrots and beans—a bit of everything!" Every evening, not one carrot was left in Coco's bowl.

Mom hugged Coco close. "Your strength rose when you ate soup too, didn't it?" Just as dough rises when everything goes in, strength grows when you eat everything. In Mom's arms, Coco called, "Not just bread—soup too! Yum, yum!"
